newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: Bolivia president promises tin sale will go ahead.
newsitem.headline: Bolivia president promises tin sale will go ahead.

text.p: Bolivia's President Gonzalo Sanchez de Lozada promised Monday that tin smelting firm Empresa Metalurgica Vinto will be privatized before he finishes his term of office in August.

The sale of Vinto, the last part of an ambitious privatization program, was postponed at the last minute last week after a dispute with unemployed miners led one bidder - Brazil's Paranapanema -- to pull out.
Sanchez de Lozada said in the Andean region of Oruro that the government would probably call a new tender this week and transfer the tin and antimony smelter to private hands within a month.
About 200 jobless workers occupied the Mount Posokini zone of the state-owned Huanuni tin mine two weeks ago calling for small mine concessions, which the government refused to grant.

Four companies were shortlisted last year to bid in the privatization tender for Vinto: Australia's Renison Goldfields Consolidated; Glencore International of Switzerland; Smelting Corp Berhad of Malaysia and Paranapanema.
Vinto has the capacity to produce 30,000 tonnes a year of tin and 7,000 tonnes of antimony.
Apart from its Bolivian supplies from state-owned mines and small producers, Vinto also tolls tin concentrates from Peru's Minsur into metal.
The winner of the tender will also be awarded control of the government's Huanuni and Colquiri tin mines.
The winner will be the firm which commits itself to make the largest investments in Vinto.

In return, the government plans to award 50 percent of Vinto to private hands, as well as administrative control. The other shares will be used to finance a new private pension fund system and divided among adult Bolivian citizens.
Firms have pledged to invest a total $1.6 billion in the privatizations of the state's railway, electricity, oil, and telecommunications companies, as well as its airline.
